- **Outcome:** Apple sees exactly the user’s active calendars, names, colors, and privileges.

- **Outcome:** One existing non-recurring timed event appears in Apple without export.
- **Depends on:** T03.

- **Changes:** Add migration/repository mapping; serialize supported VEVENT; expose resource metadata/content.
- **Out of scope:** REPORT, writes, recurrence, all-day.
- **Acceptance:** URL/UID stay stable; ETag reflects canonical content; GET is valid VCALENDAR; HEAD matches headers without body.

## T05 — Bounded calendar query

- **Outcome:** A clean client retrieves multiple timed events in a requested range.

- **Scope:** `REPORT calendar-query`, minimal XML/filter parser, limits.
- **Changes:** Return matching href, ETag, and calendar data through the DAV service.
- **Out of scope:** Multiget, recurrence expansion, unsupported filters.
- **Acceptance:** Correct inclusion/exclusion; malformed/unsupported queries fail deterministically; bounds are enforced.
- **Verify:** Parser and HTTP tests for empty, mixed, malformed, and oversized requests.

## T06 — Calendar multiget

- **Outcome:** Apple hydrates selected resources after discovery.
- **Depends on:** T05.
- **Scope:** Bounded `REPORT calendar-multiget` within one authorized collection.
- **Changes:** Parse hrefs, bulk-resolve resources, return per-resource DAV statuses.
- **Out of scope:** Writes, cross-collection batches, sync tokens.
- **Acceptance:** Existing hrefs return data/ETags; missing ones return per-item 404; foreign paths leak nothing; list size is bounded.
- **Verify:** Parser/service/HTTP tests including mixed success and authorization.
- **Handoff:** T07 assumes hydration; T15 expands authorization.

## T07 — Create from Apple

- **Outcome:** An Apple timed-event create immediately creates the same Happening event.
- **Depends on:** T06.
- **Scope:** Conditional `PUT` with `If-None-Match`, VEVENT parser, EventService create.
- **Changes:** Validate/map one VEVENT, create through domain services, persist DAV state, return Location/ETag.
- **Out of scope:** Updates, recurrence, all-day, attendee scheduling.
- **Acceptance:** Valid create is visible in both systems; duplicate/stale create fails; audit/notification behavior remains; partial writes roll back.
- **Verify:** Service/HTTP tests and end-to-end create/read proof.
- **Handoff:** Document normalization and transaction boundary.

## T08 — Conflict-safe update

- **Outcome:** Apple edits do not overwrite a newer Happening change.

- **Scope:** Existing-resource `PUT`, `If-Match`, canonical update, ETag rotation.
- **Changes:** Route through EventService and atomically compare preconditions/update DAV state.
- **Out of scope:** Delete, recurrence, all-day, merge UI.

- **Outcome:** Apple deletion removes the event and leaves durable evidence for other clients.
- **Depends on:** T08.
- **Scope:** Conditional `DELETE`, EventService delete, tombstone/revision.
- **Changes:** Enforce ETag and atomically delete while retaining the DAV mapping tombstone.
- **Out of scope:** Sync REPORT and calendar deletion.

- **Out of scope:** Moves, occurrences, imported feeds, sync response.

- **Out of scope:** Uninstrumented moves/occurrences and push notifications.

- **Outcome:** No supported Happening mutation bypasses DAV sync.
- **Depends on:** T11.

- **Changes:** Inventory all mutation entry points and route/instrument each through the recorder.
- **Out of scope:** Recurrence serialization and writes to read-only imports.

- **Out of scope:** Recurrence and floating timed events.

- **Changes:** Apply one authorization projection to discovery, reads, reports, PUT, DELETE.

# Product: Connected Apple Calendar

## Problem
People who use Happening and Apple Calendar currently have to export events one
at a time. The exported copies become detached: later edits and cancellations do
not follow, and changes made in Apple Calendar do not return to Happening. People
want to connect their Happening account once and then use the same calendars from
either application without repeating an export workflow.

## Success metric
At least 80% of people who start Apple Calendar connection complete their first
successful synchronization within 10 minutes, measured from “Start connection”
to the first confirmed calendar refresh during the first four weeks after launch.

## Announcement — the blog post before the feature
Happening now connects to Apple Calendar as an account. Connect once and the
Happening calendars you can access appear automatically in Apple Calendar across
your devices. Create, edit, move, or cancel an event in either place and the
change follows to the other. You can review the connection status or disconnect
it at any time, and Happening never asks for your Apple Account password.

# Product: Connected Apple Calendar

## Problem
People who use Happening and Apple Calendar currently have to export events one
at a time. The exported copies become detached: later edits and cancellations do
not follow, and changes made in Apple Calendar do not return to Happening. People
want to connect their Happening account once and then use the same calendars from
either application without repeating an export workflow.

## Success metric
At least 80% of people who start Apple Calendar connection complete their first
successful synchronization within 10 minutes, measured from “Start connection”
to the first confirmed calendar refresh during the first four weeks after launch.

## Announcement — the blog post before the feature
Happening now connects to Apple Calendar as an account. Connect once and the
Happening calendars you can access appear automatically in Apple Calendar across
your devices. Create, edit, move, or cancel an event in either place and the
change follows to the other. You can review the connection status or disconnect
it at any time, and Happening never asks for your Apple Account password.

## Screens
- `mockups/apple-calendar-connection.html` — account settings showing disconnected, setup, connected, attention, and disconnect states

## Product boundaries
- The connection is account-level: all Happening calendars visible to the person
  become available in Apple Calendar, subject to their existing Happening access.
- Synchronization is two-way for calendars where the person can edit events.
- Read-only Happening calendars remain read-only when viewed from Apple Calendar.
- Synchronization is automatic after setup; exact refresh timing remains under the
  calendar applications' control.
- Existing one-event downloads remain available as a convenience but are not part
  of the connected experience.
- Importing unrelated iCloud calendars into Happening is outside this feature.
